title: Norman England
capsule: Norman England designates the period following William the Conqueror's victory at the Battle of Hastings on 14 October 1066, when the Norman duchy imposed a new French-speaking aristocracy, ecclesiastical hierarchy, and administrative apparatus — exemplified by the Domesday Book survey of 1086 — over the Anglo-Saxon substrate. William's campaigns of 1069–1070 (the Harrying of the North) violently suppressed northern resistance and entrenched Norman castle-based lordship across England; his successors William Rufus and Henry I consolidated the cross-Channel Angevin realm. The period ends conventionally around 1154 with the Angevin succession, but this dataset's 1072–1169 window encompasses the completion of the initial conquest and the full Norman administrative settlement before the Becket controversy and the loss of Normandy's direct dynastic identity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. England's territorial extent in this period is well documented; the precise boundaries of royal versus baronial versus ecclesiastical control within England are recorded in Domesday and subsequent surveys.
